findings.criterion: no dead control; open/run/stop/restart and Doctor/attach either work end-to-end or fail with a named user-visible state
findings.section: Phase 2 — Capability Inventory (Evidence-by-transcript rule)
findings.message: The inventory treats a single positive side-effect transcript (curl/CLI/REPL) as sufficient for EXISTS → “wire it.” That is confirmation sampling, not a capability proof. A dead UI control is exactly the case where a backend can be prodded once and the bound button still no-ops, races, or hits a different code path. There is no required negative control (wrong args, expired session, mid-run kill), no same-path replay after UI bind, and no rule that the transcript must exercise the *same* function:line the control will call. Under this standard, STUB and EXISTS are not observationally distinct enough to stop shipping an enabled corpse.

findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars; surfaces that claim usage either work end-to-end or fail with named state (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero)
findings.section: Phase 1 — Rollup correctness spot-check; Phase 0 cost_state ↔ isolation
findings.message: The plan front-loads a *policy choice* before seeing the spot-check result: wrong numbers may “block,” ship under “provisional data,” or spin out. “Provisional” is not a North Star state. A wrong dollar (or a subscription label glued onto a real zero that was never classified) is fabricated cost whether or not a disclaimer string is nearby. Pre-authorizing a cosmetic ship path under mid-build pressure is the honesty failure the draft claims to prevent. Either wrong rollups hard-block surfacing of dollars, or the cost claim is renegotiated out of scope—there is no third honest option.

findings.criterion: usage surfaces work end-to-end or named failure; silent zero / mislabelled empty forbidden
findings.section: Success criteria (SC-3); Phase 2 — Rollup evidence gate
findings.message: SC-3 still contracts “render **existing** rollups.” Phase 1 correctly says “existing” is unverified until query + row count + sample row. Those two statements cannot both be the acceptance bar. If inventory finds empty/unreachable rollups, the conditional “aggregate + surface” split is optional re-scope, not a rewrite of SC-3. A build can still GREEN SC-3 by rendering empty accessors with honest labels while John meets silent/mislabelled zeros relative to real work—or by never creating the aggregation wave at all. Success criteria must be conditional on the evidence gate, not written as if the evidence already succeeded.

findings.criterion: Steward conversational proof is S1, not a silent claim; no dead control / silent zero / mislabelled empty / raw-binary preview
findings.section: Phase 6 — S1; Deferred remediation of S1 findings
findings.message: S1 is “the only gate authorized to declare the North Star met,” yet remediation of S1 findings is explicitly deferred to follow-on work. There is no decision rule that forbids a “North Star met” verdict while free-traversal findings still include dead controls, silent zeros, or binary dumps. Free-traversal without a pass/fail threshold is sampling theater: findings can be logged, triaged, and still left open while the verdict artifact stamps success. That recreates the exact failure mode the North Star forbids—NS declared by process, not by lived absence of the forbidden states.

findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named user-visible state
findings.section: Phase 5 — Sweep/audit; written reconciliation deferred late
findings.message: The plan admits the ten criteria are a proxy, then funds the full-surface obligation only as a late Phase 4/5 “fix-or-document” audit, with reconciliation of the proxy gap (“narrow NS or fund sweep”) also late. “Document with reason” for an in-scope health/usage/diagnose surface is not a named *user-visible* runtime state—it is a planning artifact John does not meet when he clicks. Until the North Star is either narrowed *before* surface waves or the inventory of claiming surfaces is in the acceptance set for GREEN, the build is structurally free to meet ten criteria while leaving claiming surfaces dishonest. Skeptical research standard: scope must be fixed before you collect evidence that you “met” it.

findings.criterion: no silent zero / mislabelled empty; cost never fabricates dollars
findings.section: Phase 1 — Rollup correctness spot-check
findings.message: One known session, hand-computed once, is not a correctness study of usage/time/cost rollups. It cannot speak to multi-engine sessions, zero-token runs, subscription-covered vs measured, partial sessions, or post-stop lag—the exact shapes that produce silent zeros and fake $0.00. The plan then generalizes that single comparison into surfacing policy for dashboard, tiles, and chrome. That is overclaim from under-sampling. At minimum the gate needs stratified cases (empty, zero, partial, multi-engine, failed measurement) *before* any surface is allowed to claim numbers.

findings.criterion: Doctor diagnose works end-to-end or named failure; no dead/theater control
findings.section: Phase 4 — Doctor wave; Phase 2 — diagnostic depth taxonomy
findings.message: Depth labels (credential_present / auth_round_trip / minimal_live_call / …) are assigned “from what the code actually does,” then the wave asserts the UI shows those labels. That is circular: the system grades itself by its own taxonomy. Forced wrong-key → red only falsifies “always green”; it does not prove a “live call OK” string was earned by a live call rather than a shallow probe renamed upward. Without an external oracle (captured request to the real provider, transcript of a distinguishing side effect per claimed depth, or a probe the harness controls), Doctor can still be theater with better labels—the dead/lying diagnose surface the North Star names.

findings.criterion: no dead control after open/run/stop/restart/Doctor/attach work
findings.section: Phase 2 — inventory; Phase 4 — surface waves
findings.message: EXISTS is a snapshot from Phase 1 against “John’s real v1.2.” Surface waves then change handlers, serializers, migrations, and routes. There is no requirement to re-run the transcript protocol on the *post-change* path before the wave’s end-to-end trace is accepted, nor to invalidate inventory rows when commits touch the cited file:line. Research that freezes capability truth at t0 while the system mutates is how you ship a control that was live in inventory and dead at S1.

findings.criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
findings.section: Phase 1 — shared-artifact ledger; collaborator smoke-check
findings.message: The ledger demands yes/no + named isolation mechanism, but isolation *implementation* is deferred to the first wave that writes the artifact, and the collaborator check is a named person/procedure field in EXECUTION-LOG—not a falsifiable invariant (schema version pin, flag default, binary path, DB name). “Recorded smoke outcome” can be a one-line “OK” with no artifact. That is process evidence, not isolation evidence. Under skeptical standards, “nothing ships to v1.1.x” is unproven until each shared write has a failing test if the isolation mechanism is off/mis-aimed—not a checklist cell.

findings.criterion: no silent zero / mislabelled empty; claiming surfaces work or named state (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero)
findings.section: Phase 2 — Cadence ownership; Phase 3 — as_of; Phase 4 — Cadence wave
findings.message: Rollups get query + row count + sample row. Cadence/telemetry does not: ownership is “found,” then as_of stamps and staleness UI are built as if a live telemetry stream exists. If the deployment has no supervised producer, the plan prefers poll/pull—but still treats “live telemetry on a timer” (SC-8) as the criterion. Without a Phase 1 evidence gate (who emits, at what interval, last event age, empty vs dead), frozen numbers with a pretty “as of” are still silent zeros wearing a timestamp.

findings.criterion: open, run, stop, restart real work including Doctor and attach; S1 against named task
findings.section: Phase 1 — reproducible verification task; Success criteria / S1
findings.message: The plan’s entire empirical program hangs on a concrete triple (path, command, duration) that exercises Claude, Gemini, and Grok long enough for stop/restart—and on dated confirmation John can run it *today*. The draft still only *requires* that name; it does not contain it. Until the triple exists as plan text (not a Phase 0 homework item), Doctor’s “three live subjects,” stop/summary meaningfulness, practical-usefulness windows, and S1 free-traversal are unfalsifiable promises. A research plan that postpones its only instrument is not ready to gate a remediation build.

findings.criterion: controls work end-to-end or named failure—not bound-handler theater
findings.section: Phase 4 — Universal wave acceptance standard
findings.message: The draft correctly bans “handler was called” as evidence, then accepts “click → handler → capability → side effect, captured as an artifact” without defining artifact schema: required fields, who captures it, how side effect is observed (DB row, file, provider receipt, process state), and how flaky or partial traces fail the gate. Without that, agents will attach logs that *look* end-to-end. Skeptical bar: specify the observable that would be absent if the control were dead, and require that observable in the artifact—not a narrative of the click.

findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars
findings.section: Success criteria SC-3; Phase 4 usage/cost wave
findings.message: SC-3 and the usage wave still say `cost_usd == 0` renders as `(subscription)` with a reason. Phase 2 bans inferring subscription from literal zero in code—but the success criterion itself *is* that inference unless `cost_state` (or equivalent) is already known. If migration/backfill defaults historical rows to `unmeasured`, surfacing them as subscription is fabricated dollars. The plan must make SC-3 read “render by cost_state only; numeric zero never chooses the label,” or the lint gate fights the criterion and the criterion will win at acceptance time.

findings.criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero as user-visible states; S1 not silent claim
findings.section: Phase 3/4 — screenshots; Phase 6 — visual distinguishability
findings.message: The plan repeatedly warns that GREEN does not certify visual distinguishability, then still uses screenshots as “human-verification artifacts” without requiring a human sign-off before the wave closes. That leaves a research gap: machine-attached images are not human review. Either wave close requires a dated human attestation on distinguishability, or screenshots must be demoted to debug aids and only S1 counts—today the draft implies both and therefore neither.

findings.criterion: named user-visible states for health/usage/diagnose/attach failures
findings.section: Phase 4 — per-wave fault-induction; failure-state tables
findings.message: “Induce three unlisted faults” is better than nothing but is not research on the failure modes John actually hits. Tables will overfit the harness’s imagination (bogus id, blocked port) and miss real flattener paths. Accept as incomplete method: require that Phase 1 attach/Doctor traces seed the initial table from *observed* production signals (logs from real v1.2), with induction only as coverage expansion—not as the primary discovery process.

findings.criterion: n/a
findings.section: Phase headers (“Phase 1 — Phase 0”, etc.)
findings.message: Numbering “Phase N — Phase N−1” invites wrong wave ordering and wrong EXECUTION-LOG references. Fix labels for operability; it does not itself create a dead control or fabricated dollar.

findings.criterion: John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach — without meeting a dead control
findings.section: Phase 2 — Capability Inventory (three-way reclassification); Phase 4 Deferred
findings.message: A competitor does not “win honesty” by greying out Diagnose, Retry, or Restart with a reason string. Your inventory’s third exit — “not available on this build” rendered as a named disabled state — is framed as North-Star compliant, and Phase 4 explicitly defers building ABSENT capabilities out of this effort. That is competitive surrender dressed as integrity. The North Star is not “never see a lying button”; it is that John can attach and diagnose and restart. If Phase 1 transcripts return STUB/ABSENT for Retry, Diagnose, or any restart context SC-1 treats as in-scope, this plan’s default is to ship a disabled control and call the criterion met. A rival product ships the missing capability (or drops the surface entirely so John never goes looking for it). Disabled-with-reason is still a control that does not work. Force a hard fork at inventory time: for every North-Star-named control (attach Retry, Doctor Diagnose, the single restart path SC-1/SC-5 require), the only legal outcomes are “wire it” or “build it” with a sequenced wave — never “not available on this build” without an explicit North-Star amendment John signs that those verbs are out of v1.2.

findings.criterion: open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work … without meeting a dead control; SC-5 one restart control
findings.section: Success criteria SC-1/SC-5; Phase 2 Restart-context enumeration; Phase 4 Restart waves + Deferred
findings.message: Competitors ship one obvious restart. Your success criteria promise “a single restart control” and “one restart control,” then Phase 2 and Phase 4 proudly refuse unification — every context keeps its own label, preserved/lost contract, and confirmation dialog. That is not competitor-grade UX; it is inventory theater that leaves John meeting several restart-shaped controls with different blast radii, exactly the “which one do I press?” failure mode that produces dead or terrifying controls in real use. You cannot claim SC-1/SC-5’s “single restart control” while the plan’s near-term specifics say unification is “explicitly NOT attempted.” Either collapse to one primary restart (others not shown or nested under an advanced disclosure with a single entry point), or amend SC-1/SC-5 and the North Star’s “restart” verb to admit multi-control restart — and accept that you are shipping below the bar the criteria already wrote.

findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero)
findings.section: Phase 5 — Sweep/Audit; Deferred “documented-with-reason is a valid close”
findings.message: Competitors fix or remove lying telemetry surfaces. Your Phase 4/5 audit says surfaces outside the ten criteria may close as “document with reason,” and “silence is not” the only disallowed outcome — documentation is. Documentation in a ledger does not change the DOM. A surface that still claims usage/health/diagnose and still shows blank, fake zero, or undifferentiated empty remains a North-Star violation the moment John opens it, whether or not EXECUTION-LOG has a paragraph. The North Star’s “every surface that claims…” is product-wide, not “every surface in the ten criteria.” Competitor-grade close is only: make the surface honest (named state or real data), or stop it from claiming (hide/remove the claim). “Documented known-bad claim still rendered” is an audit pass that ships a competitive loss. Tighten the audit contract: any surface that still claims health, usage, or diagnose after the sweep must either consume the named-state primitive end-to-end or stop claiming; markdown alone is not a close.

findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars
findings.section: Success criteria SC-3; Phase 4 Usage/time/cost wave; vs Phase 3 cost_state + zero-inference lint
findings.message: A competitor that has been burned by billing UI never maps a raw numeric zero to “subscription.” SC-3 and the usage wave still say `cost_usd == 0` renders as `(subscription)` with a reason. That is the same fabricated-dollar class the plan’s own Phase 3 lint exists to ban (`0 ⇒ subscription` inference forbidden). Zero is not a cost_state; it is a number that can mean subscription-covered, free tier, bug, unmeasured defaulted to 0, or a rollup that never ran. Shipping SC-3 as written reintroduces the competitor failure mode (Cursor/IDE cost tiles that show $0.00 or “included” when the meter is simply empty). Make the render path cost_state-only: subscription_covered / free_tier / measured / unmeasured / measurement_failed. Numeric zero may render only when cost_state == measured and the amount is actually zero — never as a synonym for subscription.

findings.criterion: without … a preview that dumps raw binary; SC-6 human-friendly Word/PPTX/Excel/PDF
findings.section: Phase 2 Office/PDF strategy; Phase 4 Preview wave + Deferred rich inline rendering
findings.message: Competitors (and your own “working new-window path”) give human-readable document preview. The plan allows Phase 1 to pick “download to open” as the honest strategy and then defers rich inline Office/PDF as backlog while still claiming SC-6. “Binary file — N bytes, download” is better than a hex dump, but it is not “human-friendly Word/PPTX/Excel/PDF” — it is “no preview.” A rival that reuses the new-window renderer you already admit works will look finished while v1.2 looks like a file manager. If the North Star and SC-6 mean readable preview, “download to open” is a scope cut that must amend SC-6 and the North Star’s preview clause, not a silent strategy choice. If they mean “never dump raw binary,” say that and stop marketing download as satisfying human-friendly document preview.

findings.criterion: Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build; John can … without meeting a dead control…
findings.section: Phase 6 S1; Deferred remediation of S1 findings
findings.message: Competitors treat lived validation failures as release blockers, not a parking lot. You correctly refuse silent North-Star claims until S1, then gut that discipline: S1 findings are “routed and triaged,” fixes are “follow-on,” and remediation is explicitly deferred. Structurally the build can sit at “ten criteria met; North Star pending S1,” John free-traverses into a dead control or silent zero, and the plan’s answer is a ticket — while the product John is using remains non-compliant. That is competitor-grade process theater: the only gate authorized to declare the North Star met can return FAIL and still leave the effort without a required rework loop into Phase 3/4. Define S1 FAIL ⇒ no North-Star met stamp and mandatory re-entry waves for any finding that hits a North-Star verb (dead control, silent zero, mislabelled empty, raw binary, fabricated cost, attach/Doctor). “Follow-on under renegotiation” without blocking the North-Star claim is how a competitor’s user keeps a broken build while your status board looks adult.

findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars; unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; surfaces that claim usage either work end-to-end or fail with a named state
findings.section: Phase 1 Rollup correctness spot-check policy options
findings.message: Pre-deciding that wrong rollup numbers may “ship behind a provisional data label” is a competitor anti-pattern: stick a badge on false usage/cost and call it honest. Wrong dollars with a footnote are still fabricated dollars. Wrong token counts with “provisional” still train John to distrust every tile. The only competitor-safe policies if the spot-check fails are: block the surfacing wave, spin aggregation into its own wave before any claim, or render unmeasured/measurement_failed with no numeric amount. Delete “provisional data” as a legal ship path for cost/usage claims on v1.2, or you will green a surface that lies more politely than $0.00.

findings.criterion: open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work … without meeting a dead control
findings.section: Phase 2 Stop-time inventory contingency; Phase 4 Stop-summary wave
findings.message: Competitors treat stop/restart as a pair: stop must leave enough state that restart is real work resumption, not “press restart and hope.” You allow a GREEN stop tile that says partial output was not retained, and only optionally spin checkpointing if inventory is empty — as a “larger separately-planned wave.” That contingency is the actual product. Without it, restart is a dead or hollow control even when the button is wired: John stops, sees a thin confession, restarts, and loses the run’s meaning. A rival that checkpoints mid-run wins the North Star verbs. Make the checkpoint contingency non-optional when inventory cannot support a restart that re-enters real work: either fund “checkpoint partial state during runs” as a hard dependency of SC-5 restart, or redefine restart quality so “restart from zero with a summary epitaph” is an explicit North-Star amendment — not an acceptable thin state hidden under SC-5 GREEN.

findings.criterion: Doctor diagnose … works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state; every surface that claims … diagnose
findings.section: Phase 2 diagnostic depth taxonomy; Phase 4 Doctor wave
findings.message: Competitor “doctor/diagnose” surfaces either prove the engine path or fail loudly. Your taxonomy elevates credential_present / auth_round_trip / none to first-class depth labels beside “live call,” and the wave celebrates strings like “Grok: credentials present, not exercised.” That is honesty relative to theater, but it is also a competitive tell: John asked for diagnose and received a keychain check with green-adjacent chrome. SC-4 says “real diagnosis (not shell/seed/plan-only theater)” and independent per-engine report — a credentials-only path is still theater if the control is labelled Diagnose. Competitor bar: Diagnose either performs the minimal live call/capability probe per engine or the control must not claim “diagnose” (use “check credentials” / “no diagnostic available”). Depth labels are not a free pass for success-shaped non-diagnoses. Require that any engine still in the Diagnose control’s success path reaches at least minimal_live_call, or force that engine into the explicit fourth state without a pass/fail glow.

findings.criterion: without meeting a dead control, a silent zero, a mislabelled empty, or a preview that dumps raw binary
findings.section: Phase structure (0→1→2 enabling before any Phase 3 surface); universal E2E standard
findings.message: Competitors kill the worst dead control first and dogfood the honesty vocabulary on one surface before building a platform. You forbid every surface wave until inventory + shared vocabulary + cost_state migration + tri-state harness + fault injection + screenshot tooling are GREEN. That is elegant systems work; it is also how John keeps living with dead Retry/Diagnose and raw binary preview for the entire duration of Phase 0–2, while a rival ships attach honesty alone in a day and learns what the harness must actually assert. The North Star is lived absence of those failures, not a beautiful conformance framework. Reorder for competitive risk: allow one thin “pathfinder” surface wave (attach honesty or preview binary-block — highest daily pain) after Capability Inventory rows for that control only, with a disposable assertion set, then generalize into shared harnesses. Full Phase 2 before any user-visible fix optimizes for process purity and against the North Star’s daily verbs.

findings.criterion: surfaces that claim health/usage work end-to-end or fail with named state; SC-8 cadence is real from live telemetry
findings.section: Phase 2 Cadence ownership; Phase 4 Cadence wave
findings.message: Competitors with “live” usage/health either push or poll on a supervised timer and show staleness when the feed dies. Preferring pull-on-render when no supervised owner exists can still satisfy “not prose that looks like a scheduler,” but it loses to products whose tiles move without a full page re-render. If pull-on-render is chosen, competitor-grade honesty requires the as_of/staleness primitive to be unavoidable (you partly have this) and a visible “updates only on refresh” contract so John does not think he bought live cadence. Without that contract, SC-8’s “cadence is real” overclaims relative to the implementation you pre-authorize.

findings.criterion: attach and Doctor diagnose without dead control / mislabelled empty; named user-visible states
findings.section: Phase 2–4 surface waves (acceptance standards)
findings.message: The plan invents reason enums and depth taxonomies in a vacuum. Competitors (session reconnect in agent IDEs, provider health in multi-model routers) already teach users what timeout vs dead session vs auth failure looks like. Without a one-page “parity bar” — minimum distinguishable outcomes attach and Doctor must match — your distinct strings can be technically non-collapsing and still unreadable next to a rival’s. This is refinement, not a new product: add a short competitor-outcome table (timeout, ended, unauthorized, transport, per-engine diagnose fail) that acceptance strings must be at least as distinguishable as, before inventing novel vocabulary.

findings.criterion: n/a
findings.section: All phase headings
findings.message: Labelling “Phase 1 — Phase 0”, “Phase 4 — Phase 3”, etc. is competitive amateur hour for anyone skimming the plan. It does not break the North Star, but it burns trust before Wave 1. Pick one numbering scheme.

findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach — without meeting a dead control
findings.section: Phase 1–3 framing (Phases 0–2); intro
findings.message: Phases 0–2 are explicitly zero product code — inventories, transcripts, harnesses, migrations, lints — and the draft forbids surface waves until all of that is GREEN. A bored investor funds working Retry, Diagnose, Stop, and Restart, not a Capability Inventory table. The plan has no calendar bound, no wave-count cap, and no interim “ship one live control” milestone before the enabling stack. If inventory or harness work expands (coverage toolchain wave, cost_state migration, checkpoint contingency), every North-Star surface stays dead while the build looks busy. Refute the sequencing as capital-blind until the plan names a hard pre-surface budget and at least one user-visible control that must land before more machinery is funded.

findings.criterion: open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work … without meeting a dead control
findings.section: Success criteria SC-1 / SC-5; Phase 2 restart enumeration; Phase 4 restart waves
findings.message: Success criteria require “a single restart control — work or not shown” and SC-5 again says “one restart control.” Phase 2 then enumerates multiple restart contexts and Phase 4 states unification is “explicitly NOT attempted.” That is not refinement of the same promise — it is a contradiction. Either the criterion is wrong or the wave design is wrong. As written, the build can GREEN several labelled restart buttons with partial contracts and still fail the success bar the plan itself set, while John meets a control zoo that looks alive and behaves inconsistently. Resolve the contract in writing before any restart wave is scoped: one control, or many with “not shown” for the rest — not both.

findings.criterion: without meeting a dead control … Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.section: Phase 2 — three-way reclassification; Phase 4 deferred ABSENT
findings.message: Reclassification to “not available on this build” (named disabled + reason) is allowed for Retry, Diagnose, restart contexts, and anything ABSENT in inventory. That is an honest UI pattern, but the draft sets no floor on which North-Star controls may be voided, no John-approval gate before voiding, and no rule that “build it” is mandatory for controls the success criteria name. Inventory can therefore convert the entire defect-remediation thesis into a catalogue of disabled buttons, ship GREEN process waves, and leave John unable to attach, diagnose, or restart. A bored investor calls that a plan to document failure, not fix it. Require an explicit non-voidable control set (at least Retry, Diagnose, Stop, one Restart, Doctor handoff, cost honesty path) that may only be reduced by logged renegotiation with John — never by inventory fiat.

findings.criterion: John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work
findings.section: Success criteria; Phase 4 surface list; intro Phase 3 list
findings.message: The North Star leads with open and run. The surface phase lists attach honesty, usage/cost, Doctor, stop/restart, preview, projects-collapsed, cadence — not open or run. Those verbs only appear in S1 free-traversal and the Phase 4 sweep inventory. That means the plan can spend the bulk of remediation budget on collapsed folders and cadence timers while open/run dead controls are “fix-or-document” leftovers. From a capital view, you are funding second-order chrome before the verbs the North Star names first. Add first-class open/run waves (or an explicit inventory row proving they already work end-to-end with transcripts) before funding SC-7/SC-8.

findings.criterion: stop, and restart real Anchor work … without meeting a dead control
findings.section: Phase 2 stop-time inventory; Phase 4 stop-summary wave
findings.message: If stop-time inventory finds nothing meaningful retained, the draft escalates to “checkpoint partial state during runs” — “a larger separately-planned wave” with sizing deferred. Stop-summary then depends on that wave. There is no size cap, no decision deadline, and no honest fallback that still satisfies “stopping leaves a tile summarizing in-flight work” if checkpointing is declined. That is an open-ended option to never finish stop/restart under budget pressure. Pre-write the kill switch: either fund checkpointing inside this effort with a fixed scope, or ship a named thin summary state that does not claim retained work it does not have — and treat full checkpointing as renegotiated out-of-effort, not an infinite dependency.

findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars … unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero
findings.section: Phase 1 cost_state isolation; rollup spot-check policy; Phase 3 cost_state migration deferred
findings.message: Phase 0 pre-decides that wrong rollups may “block,” “ship behind a provisional data label,” or “spin out” — chosen before seeing numbers, but still allowing a ship path that is not full honesty. Separately, if branch isolation rejects the additive column, the plan says cost honesty “cannot be fully met” and may be scoped down rather than met “cosmetically at the render layer.” A bored investor hears two legal paths to partial cost truth while success criteria still promise cost_usd==0 never renders as $0.00 and unmeasured never looks like zero. “Provisional” and “scoped down” are not defined against fabricate-vs-unknown. Lock a single fail-closed rule: no dollar amount renders unless cost_state is measured; subscription/free/unmeasured/failed are labels without fabricated $; provisional is forbidden as a display class unless it is identical to unmeasured/unknown and never a dollar figure.

findings.criterion: Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build
findings.section: Phase 6 S1; deferred remediation of S1 findings
findings.message: S1 is correctly the only gate authorized to declare the North Star met, and status stays “ten criteria met; North Star pending S1.” But S1 findings are explicitly not remediated in this effort — they are routed as follow-on under renegotiation. That means the plan can manufacture a permanent parking state: automated GREEN, S1 failed or never clean, North Star never claimed, and no obligation to burn the remaining capital to close the gap S1 found. A steward proof that cannot force a fix loop is theater with a timestamp. Specify that a failed S1 either (a) reopens named waves inside this effort until S1 passes or John logs a North-Star amendment, or (b) terminal status is “effort failed North Star” — not an indefinite “pending S1” that looks like almost-done.

findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.section: Phase 2 conditional scope-change; three-way reclassification ‘build it’; intro dependency order
findings.message: Empty rollups flip a surface wave into “aggregate + surface” as a new wave; ABSENT capabilities each get their own wave; stop may spawn checkpointing; coverage may spawn a toolchain wave. None of these expansions has a total-wave ceiling, a cut-line, or a “prefer named unavailable over unbounded build” default for non-core surfaces. Under real budget, expansion waves crowd out Doctor, attach, and cost honesty — the exact surfaces the North Star names. Write a hard expansion budget (max new waves / max reclassified build-its without renegotiation) and a priority order that always funds attach, Doctor, stop/restart, and cost honesty before projects-collapsed, cadence polish, or opportunistic aggregation.

findings.criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
findings.section: Phase 1 shared-artifact ledger; collaborator smoke-check protocol; Phase 4/5 checklist lines
findings.message: Isolation is “named per artifact” and collaborator smoke is “triggered after any wave that modified a shared artifact.” The draft never says what happens if the named collaborator is unavailable, late, or the check is skipped: block the wave, block the release, or note “smoke not run.” A process field with no fail-closed outcome is a checkbox investors ignore and builds skip. Without a mechanical block on shared-artifact writes until smoke returns pass (or John signs a written isolation exception), “nothing ships to v1.1.x” remains an aspiration the EXECUTION-LOG can paper over with an empty field.

findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.section: Phase 5 proxy reconciliation; Phase 2 control-and-surface sweep; intro Phase 4
findings.message: The draft admits the ten criteria are a proxy and that the North Star is wider, then postpones “narrow the North Star or fund the sweep” until Phase 4 — after all surface waves. That is decision order inverted: you spend the remediation budget on the proxy set, then ask whether the North Star still applies. A bored investor funds one scope, once. Force the narrow-or-fund choice in Phase 0/1 before surface waves are written; otherwise Phase 4 “document with reason” will launder out-of-criteria health/usage/diagnose surfaces as accepted debt while John still hits mislabelled empties S1 is told to treat as findings.

findings.criterion: open, run, stop, restart … Doctor … session attach … S1 … not a silent claim of this build
findings.section: Phase 1 transcripts; Phase 0 verification task confirmation; Phase 6 S1
findings.message: EXISTS verdicts require live transcripts against John’s real v1.2 environment; rollup evidence needs his DB rows; the verification task needs his dated confirmation; S1 is John-only free traversal. The plan has no SLA, no parallel path, and no “blocked on human evidence” clock that forces renegotiation rather than idle swarm spend. If John is the critical path for every honesty claim, the build either fabricates evidence from code-reading (forbidden) or burns calendar with zero surface progress. Name max wait, who can produce transcripts besides John, and what ships as “unknown / not verified” rather than waiting forever for the perfect paste.

findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.section: Phase 2 inventory scope; Phase 4 surface waves; Phase 5 audit
findings.message: Usage and diagnose get dedicated waves, accessors, taxonomies, and fault sets. “Health” appears in the North Star and the Phase 4/5 sweep language but never receives a first-class inventory column, rollup evidence gate, or surface wave of its own. Health can therefore remain a silent or mislabelled surface until a late audit documents it. Either promote health to the same evidence-and-surface bar as usage/diagnose or strike it from what this effort claims — do not leave it as the unpaid third noun.

findings.criterion: without meeting a dead control, a silent zero, a mislabelled empty
findings.section: Phase 4 dual-profile verification standard
findings.message: UI-state fixes must pass on John’s existing profile, not only a clean profile — correct for preference/collapse bugs, but it makes every UI wave depend on access to his real stored state with no fixture that reproduces that profile. Without a captured profile snapshot as a first-class Phase 0 artifact, dual-profile is another serial John dependency that can stall or be quietly skipped. Capture and version the profile fixture when the verification task is named, or the dual-profile gate is not mechanically producible.

demoted.message: Numbering “Phase N — Phase N−1” invites wrong wave ordering and wrong EXECUTION-LOG references. Fix labels for operability; it does not itself create a dead control or fabricated dollar.

Labelling “Phase 1 — Phase 0”, “Phase 4 — Phase 3”, etc. is competitive amateur hour for anyone skimming the plan. It does not break the North Star, but it burns trust before Wave 1. Pick one numbering scheme.

reviews.note: Skeptical-researcher angle only. Findings target unfalsifiable evidence rules, N=1 “proof,” escape hatches that re-label dishonesty, and proxy/scope gaps that let GREEN mean something weaker than the North Star.

findings.section: Phase 2 — Capability Inventory (Evidence-by-transcript rule)
findings.criterion: no dead control; open/run/stop/restart and Doctor/attach either work end-to-end or fail with a named user-visible state
findings.message: The inventory treats a single positive side-effect transcript (curl/CLI/REPL) as sufficient for EXISTS → “wire it.” That is confirmation sampling, not a capability proof. A dead UI control is exactly the case where a backend can be prodded once and the bound button still no-ops, races, or hits a different code path. There is no required negative control (wrong args, expired session, mid-run kill), no same-path replay after UI bind, and no rule that the transcript must exercise the *same* function:line the control will call. Under this standard, STUB and EXISTS are not observationally distinct enough to stop shipping an enabled corpse.

findings.section: Phase 1 — Rollup correctness spot-check; Phase 0 cost_state ↔ isolation
findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars; surfaces that claim usage either work end-to-end or fail with named state (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero)
findings.message: The plan front-loads a *policy choice* before seeing the spot-check result: wrong numbers may “block,” ship under “provisional data,” or spin out. “Provisional” is not a North Star state. A wrong dollar (or a subscription label glued onto a real zero that was never classified) is fabricated cost whether or not a disclaimer string is nearby. Pre-authorizing a cosmetic ship path under mid-build pressure is the honesty failure the draft claims to prevent. Either wrong rollups hard-block surfacing of dollars, or the cost claim is renegotiated out of scope—there is no third honest option.

findings.topic: SC-3 assumes existing rollups while evidence gate treats them as unproven
findings.section: Success criteria (SC-3); Phase 2 — Rollup evidence gate
findings.criterion: usage surfaces work end-to-end or named failure; silent zero / mislabelled empty forbidden
findings.message: SC-3 still contracts “render **existing** rollups.” Phase 1 correctly says “existing” is unverified until query + row count + sample row. Those two statements cannot both be the acceptance bar. If inventory finds empty/unreachable rollups, the conditional “aggregate + surface” split is optional re-scope, not a rewrite of SC-3. A build can still GREEN SC-3 by rendering empty accessors with honest labels while John meets silent/mislabelled zeros relative to real work—or by never creating the aggregation wave at all. Success criteria must be conditional on the evidence gate, not written as if the evidence already succeeded.

findings.topic: S1 can declare North Star met with open defects
findings.section: Phase 6 — S1; Deferred remediation of S1 findings
findings.criterion: Steward conversational proof is S1, not a silent claim; no dead control / silent zero / mislabelled empty / raw-binary preview
findings.message: S1 is “the only gate authorized to declare the North Star met,” yet remediation of S1 findings is explicitly deferred to follow-on work. There is no decision rule that forbids a “North Star met” verdict while free-traversal findings still include dead controls, silent zeros, or binary dumps. Free-traversal without a pass/fail threshold is sampling theater: findings can be logged, triaged, and still left open while the verdict artifact stamps success. That recreates the exact failure mode the North Star forbids—NS declared by process, not by lived absence of the forbidden states.

findings.topic: proxy ten-criteria vs every health/usage/diagnose surface
findings.section: Phase 5 — Sweep/audit; written reconciliation deferred late
findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named user-visible state
findings.message: The plan admits the ten criteria are a proxy, then funds the full-surface obligation only as a late Phase 4/5 “fix-or-document” audit, with reconciliation of the proxy gap (“narrow NS or fund sweep”) also late. “Document with reason” for an in-scope health/usage/diagnose surface is not a named *user-visible* runtime state—it is a planning artifact John does not meet when he clicks. Until the North Star is either narrowed *before* surface waves or the inventory of claiming surfaces is in the acceptance set for GREEN, the build is structurally free to meet ten criteria while leaving claiming surfaces dishonest. Skeptical research standard: scope must be fixed before you collect evidence that you “met” it.

findings.topic: N=1 hand-compute as rollup correctness research
findings.section: Phase 1 — Rollup correctness spot-check
findings.criterion: no silent zero / mislabelled empty; cost never fabricates dollars
findings.message: One known session, hand-computed once, is not a correctness study of usage/time/cost rollups. It cannot speak to multi-engine sessions, zero-token runs, subscription-covered vs measured, partial sessions, or post-stop lag—the exact shapes that produce silent zeros and fake $0.00. The plan then generalizes that single comparison into surfacing policy for dashboard, tiles, and chrome. That is overclaim from under-sampling. At minimum the gate needs stratified cases (empty, zero, partial, multi-engine, failed measurement) *before* any surface is allowed to claim numbers.

findings.section: Phase 4 — Doctor wave; Phase 2 — diagnostic depth taxonomy
findings.criterion: Doctor diagnose works end-to-end or named failure; no dead/theater control
findings.message: Depth labels (credential_present / auth_round_trip / minimal_live_call / …) are assigned “from what the code actually does,” then the wave asserts the UI shows those labels. That is circular: the system grades itself by its own taxonomy. Forced wrong-key → red only falsifies “always green”; it does not prove a “live call OK” string was earned by a live call rather than a shallow probe renamed upward. Without an external oracle (captured request to the real provider, transcript of a distinguishing side effect per claimed depth, or a probe the harness controls), Doctor can still be theater with better labels—the dead/lying diagnose surface the North Star names.

findings.topic: no mid-build re-proof of inventory verdicts
findings.section: Phase 2 — inventory; Phase 4 — surface waves
findings.criterion: no dead control after open/run/stop/restart/Doctor/attach work
findings.message: EXISTS is a snapshot from Phase 1 against “John’s real v1.2.” Surface waves then change handlers, serializers, migrations, and routes. There is no requirement to re-run the transcript protocol on the *post-change* path before the wave’s end-to-end trace is accepted, nor to invalidate inventory rows when commits touch the cited file:line. Research that freezes capability truth at t0 while the system mutates is how you ship a control that was live in inventory and dead at S1.

findings.section: Phase 1 — shared-artifact ledger; collaborator smoke-check
findings.criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
findings.message: The ledger demands yes/no + named isolation mechanism, but isolation *implementation* is deferred to the first wave that writes the artifact, and the collaborator check is a named person/procedure field in EXECUTION-LOG—not a falsifiable invariant (schema version pin, flag default, binary path, DB name). “Recorded smoke outcome” can be a one-line “OK” with no artifact. That is process evidence, not isolation evidence. Under skeptical standards, “nothing ships to v1.1.x” is unproven until each shared write has a failing test if the isolation mechanism is off/mis-aimed—not a checklist cell.

findings.section: Phase 2 — Cadence ownership; Phase 3 — as_of; Phase 4 — Cadence wave
findings.criterion: no silent zero / mislabelled empty; claiming surfaces work or named state (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero)
findings.message: Rollups get query + row count + sample row. Cadence/telemetry does not: ownership is “found,” then as_of stamps and staleness UI are built as if a live telemetry stream exists. If the deployment has no supervised producer, the plan prefers poll/pull—but still treats “live telemetry on a timer” (SC-8) as the criterion. Without a Phase 1 evidence gate (who emits, at what interval, last event age, empty vs dead), frozen numbers with a pretty “as of” are still silent zeros wearing a timestamp.

findings.topic: verification task required but still unspecified
findings.section: Phase 1 — reproducible verification task; Success criteria / S1
findings.criterion: open, run, stop, restart real work including Doctor and attach; S1 against named task
findings.message: The plan’s entire empirical program hangs on a concrete triple (path, command, duration) that exercises Claude, Gemini, and Grok long enough for stop/restart—and on dated confirmation John can run it *today*. The draft still only *requires* that name; it does not contain it. Until the triple exists as plan text (not a Phase 0 homework item), Doctor’s “three live subjects,” stop/summary meaningfulness, practical-usefulness windows, and S1 free-traversal are unfalsifiable promises. A research plan that postpones its only instrument is not ready to gate a remediation build.

findings.section: Phase 4 — Universal wave acceptance standard
findings.criterion: controls work end-to-end or named failure—not bound-handler theater
findings.message: The draft correctly bans “handler was called” as evidence, then accepts “click → handler → capability → side effect, captured as an artifact” without defining artifact schema: required fields, who captures it, how side effect is observed (DB row, file, provider receipt, process state), and how flaky or partial traces fail the gate. Without that, agents will attach logs that *look* end-to-end. Skeptical bar: specify the observable that would be absent if the control were dead, and require that observable in the artifact—not a narrative of the click.

findings.section: Success criteria SC-3; Phase 4 usage/cost wave
findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars
findings.message: SC-3 and the usage wave still say `cost_usd == 0` renders as `(subscription)` with a reason. Phase 2 bans inferring subscription from literal zero in code—but the success criterion itself *is* that inference unless `cost_state` (or equivalent) is already known. If migration/backfill defaults historical rows to `unmeasured`, surfacing them as subscription is fabricated dollars. The plan must make SC-3 read “render by cost_state only; numeric zero never chooses the label,” or the lint gate fights the criterion and the criterion will win at acceptance time.

findings.section: Phase 3/4 — screenshots; Phase 6 — visual distinguishability
findings.criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero as user-visible states; S1 not silent claim
findings.message: The plan repeatedly warns that GREEN does not certify visual distinguishability, then still uses screenshots as “human-verification artifacts” without requiring a human sign-off before the wave closes. That leaves a research gap: machine-attached images are not human review. Either wave close requires a dated human attestation on distinguishability, or screenshots must be demoted to debug aids and only S1 counts—today the draft implies both and therefore neither.

findings.topic: fault-induction not a failure distribution sample
findings.section: Phase 4 — per-wave fault-induction; failure-state tables
findings.criterion: named user-visible states for health/usage/diagnose/attach failures
findings.message: “Induce three unlisted faults” is better than nothing but is not research on the failure modes John actually hits. Tables will overfit the harness’s imagination (bogus id, blocked port) and miss real flattener paths. Accept as incomplete method: require that Phase 1 attach/Doctor traces seed the initial table from *observed* production signals (logs from real v1.2), with induction only as coverage expansion—not as the primary discovery process.

findings.section: Phase headers (“Phase 1 — Phase 0”, etc.)
findings.criterion: n/a
findings.message: Numbering “Phase N — Phase N−1” invites wrong wave ordering and wrong EXECUTION-LOG references. Fix labels for operability; it does not itself create a dead control or fabricated dollar.

reviews.note: Contrarian Shark · competitor angle. Judged only against the North Star and what the draft writes. Process-bloat and “would ship faster” are kept only where they threaten a named North-Star outcome (usable open/run/stop/restart/diagnose/attach, honest states, non-fabricated cost), not velocity-for-its-own-sake.

findings.section: Phase 2 — Capability Inventory (three-way reclassification); Phase 4 Deferred
findings.criterion: John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach — without meeting a dead control
findings.message: A competitor does not “win honesty” by greying out Diagnose, Retry, or Restart with a reason string. Your inventory’s third exit — “not available on this build” rendered as a named disabled state — is framed as North-Star compliant, and Phase 4 explicitly defers building ABSENT capabilities out of this effort. That is competitive surrender dressed as integrity. The North Star is not “never see a lying button”; it is that John can attach and diagnose and restart. If Phase 1 transcripts return STUB/ABSENT for Retry, Diagnose, or any restart context SC-1 treats as in-scope, this plan’s default is to ship a disabled control and call the criterion met. A rival product ships the missing capability (or drops the surface entirely so John never goes looking for it). Disabled-with-reason is still a control that does not work. Force a hard fork at inventory time: for every North-Star-named control (attach Retry, Doctor Diagnose, the single restart path SC-1/SC-5 require), the only legal outcomes are “wire it” or “build it” with a sequenced wave — never “not available on this build” without an explicit North-Star amendment John signs that those verbs are out of v1.2.

findings.topic: one restart control vs multi-context non-unification
findings.section: Success criteria SC-1/SC-5; Phase 2 Restart-context enumeration; Phase 4 Restart waves + Deferred
findings.criterion: open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work … without meeting a dead control; SC-5 one restart control
findings.message: Competitors ship one obvious restart. Your success criteria promise “a single restart control” and “one restart control,” then Phase 2 and Phase 4 proudly refuse unification — every context keeps its own label, preserved/lost contract, and confirmation dialog. That is not competitor-grade UX; it is inventory theater that leaves John meeting several restart-shaped controls with different blast radii, exactly the “which one do I press?” failure mode that produces dead or terrifying controls in real use. You cannot claim SC-1/SC-5’s “single restart control” while the plan’s near-term specifics say unification is “explicitly NOT attempted.” Either collapse to one primary restart (others not shown or nested under an advanced disclosure with a single entry point), or amend SC-1/SC-5 and the North Star’s “restart” verb to admit multi-control restart — and accept that you are shipping below the bar the criteria already wrote.

findings.section: Phase 5 — Sweep/Audit; Deferred “documented-with-reason is a valid close”
findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero)
findings.message: Competitors fix or remove lying telemetry surfaces. Your Phase 4/5 audit says surfaces outside the ten criteria may close as “document with reason,” and “silence is not” the only disallowed outcome — documentation is. Documentation in a ledger does not change the DOM. A surface that still claims usage/health/diagnose and still shows blank, fake zero, or undifferentiated empty remains a North-Star violation the moment John opens it, whether or not EXECUTION-LOG has a paragraph. The North Star’s “every surface that claims…” is product-wide, not “every surface in the ten criteria.” Competitor-grade close is only: make the surface honest (named state or real data), or stop it from claiming (hide/remove the claim). “Documented known-bad claim still rendered” is an audit pass that ships a competitive loss. Tighten the audit contract: any surface that still claims health, usage, or diagnose after the sweep must either consume the named-state primitive end-to-end or stop claiming; markdown alone is not a close.

findings.section: Success criteria SC-3; Phase 4 Usage/time/cost wave; vs Phase 3 cost_state + zero-inference lint
findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars
findings.message: A competitor that has been burned by billing UI never maps a raw numeric zero to “subscription.” SC-3 and the usage wave still say `cost_usd == 0` renders as `(subscription)` with a reason. That is the same fabricated-dollar class the plan’s own Phase 3 lint exists to ban (`0 ⇒ subscription` inference forbidden). Zero is not a cost_state; it is a number that can mean subscription-covered, free tier, bug, unmeasured defaulted to 0, or a rollup that never ran. Shipping SC-3 as written reintroduces the competitor failure mode (Cursor/IDE cost tiles that show $0.00 or “included” when the meter is simply empty). Make the render path cost_state-only: subscription_covered / free_tier / measured / unmeasured / measurement_failed. Numeric zero may render only when cost_state == measured and the amount is actually zero — never as a synonym for subscription.

findings.section: Phase 2 Office/PDF strategy; Phase 4 Preview wave + Deferred rich inline rendering
findings.criterion: without … a preview that dumps raw binary; SC-6 human-friendly Word/PPTX/Excel/PDF
findings.message: Competitors (and your own “working new-window path”) give human-readable document preview. The plan allows Phase 1 to pick “download to open” as the honest strategy and then defers rich inline Office/PDF as backlog while still claiming SC-6. “Binary file — N bytes, download” is better than a hex dump, but it is not “human-friendly Word/PPTX/Excel/PDF” — it is “no preview.” A rival that reuses the new-window renderer you already admit works will look finished while v1.2 looks like a file manager. If the North Star and SC-6 mean readable preview, “download to open” is a scope cut that must amend SC-6 and the North Star’s preview clause, not a silent strategy choice. If they mean “never dump raw binary,” say that and stop marketing download as satisfying human-friendly document preview.

findings.topic: S1 findings not remediated before North-Star claim
findings.section: Phase 6 S1; Deferred remediation of S1 findings
findings.criterion: Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build; John can … without meeting a dead control…
findings.message: Competitors treat lived validation failures as release blockers, not a parking lot. You correctly refuse silent North-Star claims until S1, then gut that discipline: S1 findings are “routed and triaged,” fixes are “follow-on,” and remediation is explicitly deferred. Structurally the build can sit at “ten criteria met; North Star pending S1,” John free-traverses into a dead control or silent zero, and the plan’s answer is a ticket — while the product John is using remains non-compliant. That is competitor-grade process theater: the only gate authorized to declare the North Star met can return FAIL and still leave the effort without a required rework loop into Phase 3/4. Define S1 FAIL ⇒ no North-Star met stamp and mandatory re-entry waves for any finding that hits a North-Star verb (dead control, silent zero, mislabelled empty, raw binary, fabricated cost, attach/Doctor). “Follow-on under renegotiation” without blocking the North-Star claim is how a competitor’s user keeps a broken build while your status board looks adult.

findings.section: Phase 1 Rollup correctness spot-check policy options
findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars; unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; surfaces that claim usage either work end-to-end or fail with a named state
findings.message: Pre-deciding that wrong rollup numbers may “ship behind a provisional data label” is a competitor anti-pattern: stick a badge on false usage/cost and call it honest. Wrong dollars with a footnote are still fabricated dollars. Wrong token counts with “provisional” still train John to distrust every tile. The only competitor-safe policies if the spot-check fails are: block the surfacing wave, spin aggregation into its own wave before any claim, or render unmeasured/measurement_failed with no numeric amount. Delete “provisional data” as a legal ship path for cost/usage claims on v1.2, or you will green a surface that lies more politely than $0.00.

findings.topic: thin stop summary without restart utility
findings.section: Phase 2 Stop-time inventory contingency; Phase 4 Stop-summary wave
findings.criterion: open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work … without meeting a dead control
findings.message: Competitors treat stop/restart as a pair: stop must leave enough state that restart is real work resumption, not “press restart and hope.” You allow a GREEN stop tile that says partial output was not retained, and only optionally spin checkpointing if inventory is empty — as a “larger separately-planned wave.” That contingency is the actual product. Without it, restart is a dead or hollow control even when the button is wired: John stops, sees a thin confession, restarts, and loses the run’s meaning. A rival that checkpoints mid-run wins the North Star verbs. Make the checkpoint contingency non-optional when inventory cannot support a restart that re-enters real work: either fund “checkpoint partial state during runs” as a hard dependency of SC-5 restart, or redefine restart quality so “restart from zero with a summary epitaph” is an explicit North-Star amendment — not an acceptable thin state hidden under SC-5 GREEN.

findings.topic: Doctor depth labels that look like success
findings.section: Phase 2 diagnostic depth taxonomy; Phase 4 Doctor wave
findings.criterion: Doctor diagnose … works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state; every surface that claims … diagnose
findings.message: Competitor “doctor/diagnose” surfaces either prove the engine path or fail loudly. Your taxonomy elevates credential_present / auth_round_trip / none to first-class depth labels beside “live call,” and the wave celebrates strings like “Grok: credentials present, not exercised.” That is honesty relative to theater, but it is also a competitive tell: John asked for diagnose and received a keychain check with green-adjacent chrome. SC-4 says “real diagnosis (not shell/seed/plan-only theater)” and independent per-engine report — a credentials-only path is still theater if the control is labelled Diagnose. Competitor bar: Diagnose either performs the minimal live call/capability probe per engine or the control must not claim “diagnose” (use “check credentials” / “no diagnostic available”). Depth labels are not a free pass for success-shaped non-diagnoses. Require that any engine still in the Diagnose control’s success path reaches at least minimal_live_call, or force that engine into the explicit fourth state without a pass/fail glow.

findings.section: Phase structure (0→1→2 enabling before any Phase 3 surface); universal E2E standard
findings.criterion: without meeting a dead control, a silent zero, a mislabelled empty, or a preview that dumps raw binary
findings.message: Competitors kill the worst dead control first and dogfood the honesty vocabulary on one surface before building a platform. You forbid every surface wave until inventory + shared vocabulary + cost_state migration + tri-state harness + fault injection + screenshot tooling are GREEN. That is elegant systems work; it is also how John keeps living with dead Retry/Diagnose and raw binary preview for the entire duration of Phase 0–2, while a rival ships attach honesty alone in a day and learns what the harness must actually assert. The North Star is lived absence of those failures, not a beautiful conformance framework. Reorder for competitive risk: allow one thin “pathfinder” surface wave (attach honesty or preview binary-block — highest daily pain) after Capability Inventory rows for that control only, with a disposable assertion set, then generalize into shared harnesses. Full Phase 2 before any user-visible fix optimizes for process purity and against the North Star’s daily verbs.

findings.topic: client poll cadence vs live competitor telemetry
findings.section: Phase 2 Cadence ownership; Phase 4 Cadence wave
findings.criterion: surfaces that claim health/usage work end-to-end or fail with named state; SC-8 cadence is real from live telemetry
findings.message: Competitors with “live” usage/health either push or poll on a supervised timer and show staleness when the feed dies. Preferring pull-on-render when no supervised owner exists can still satisfy “not prose that looks like a scheduler,” but it loses to products whose tiles move without a full page re-render. If pull-on-render is chosen, competitor-grade honesty requires the as_of/staleness primitive to be unavoidable (you partly have this) and a visible “updates only on refresh” contract so John does not think he bought live cadence. Without that contract, SC-8’s “cadence is real” overclaims relative to the implementation you pre-authorize.

findings.topic: no external competitive bar for attach/Doctor UX
findings.section: Phase 2–4 surface waves (acceptance standards)
findings.criterion: attach and Doctor diagnose without dead control / mislabelled empty; named user-visible states
findings.message: The plan invents reason enums and depth taxonomies in a vacuum. Competitors (session reconnect in agent IDEs, provider health in multi-model routers) already teach users what timeout vs dead session vs auth failure looks like. Without a one-page “parity bar” — minimum distinguishable outcomes attach and Doctor must match — your distinct strings can be technically non-collapsing and still unreadable next to a rival’s. This is refinement, not a new product: add a short competitor-outcome table (timeout, ended, unauthorized, transport, per-engine diagnose fail) that acceptance strings must be at least as distinguishable as, before inventing novel vocabulary.

findings.topic: phase numbering Phase N — Phase N-1
findings.section: All phase headings
findings.criterion: n/a
findings.message: Labelling “Phase 1 — Phase 0”, “Phase 4 — Phase 3”, etc. is competitive amateur hour for anyone skimming the plan. It does not break the North Star, but it burns trust before Wave 1. Pick one numbering scheme.

reviews.note: Analyst Shark · bored-investor angle. Findings only where the draft risks spending the whole budget on process, escape hatches, or late decisions while John still meets dead controls, dishonest cost, or an unmet North Star. Process theater that does not touch a North-Star criterion is omitted.

findings.section: Phase 1–3 framing (Phases 0–2); intro
findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach — without meeting a dead control
findings.message: Phases 0–2 are explicitly zero product code — inventories, transcripts, harnesses, migrations, lints — and the draft forbids surface waves until all of that is GREEN. A bored investor funds working Retry, Diagnose, Stop, and Restart, not a Capability Inventory table. The plan has no calendar bound, no wave-count cap, and no interim “ship one live control” milestone before the enabling stack. If inventory or harness work expands (coverage toolchain wave, cost_state migration, checkpoint contingency), every North-Star surface stays dead while the build looks busy. Refute the sequencing as capital-blind until the plan names a hard pre-surface budget and at least one user-visible control that must land before more machinery is funded.

findings.section: Success criteria SC-1 / SC-5; Phase 2 restart enumeration; Phase 4 restart waves
findings.criterion: open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work … without meeting a dead control
findings.message: Success criteria require “a single restart control — work or not shown” and SC-5 again says “one restart control.” Phase 2 then enumerates multiple restart contexts and Phase 4 states unification is “explicitly NOT attempted.” That is not refinement of the same promise — it is a contradiction. Either the criterion is wrong or the wave design is wrong. As written, the build can GREEN several labelled restart buttons with partial contracts and still fail the success bar the plan itself set, while John meets a control zoo that looks alive and behaves inconsistently. Resolve the contract in writing before any restart wave is scoped: one control, or many with “not shown” for the rest — not both.

findings.topic: inventory can void North Star controls
findings.section: Phase 2 — three-way reclassification; Phase 4 deferred ABSENT
findings.criterion: without meeting a dead control … Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: Reclassification to “not available on this build” (named disabled + reason) is allowed for Retry, Diagnose, restart contexts, and anything ABSENT in inventory. That is an honest UI pattern, but the draft sets no floor on which North-Star controls may be voided, no John-approval gate before voiding, and no rule that “build it” is mandatory for controls the success criteria name. Inventory can therefore convert the entire defect-remediation thesis into a catalogue of disabled buttons, ship GREEN process waves, and leave John unable to attach, diagnose, or restart. A bored investor calls that a plan to document failure, not fix it. Require an explicit non-voidable control set (at least Retry, Diagnose, Stop, one Restart, Doctor handoff, cost honesty path) that may only be reduced by logged renegotiation with John — never by inventory fiat.

findings.section: Success criteria; Phase 4 surface list; intro Phase 3 list
findings.criterion: John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work
findings.message: The North Star leads with open and run. The surface phase lists attach honesty, usage/cost, Doctor, stop/restart, preview, projects-collapsed, cadence — not open or run. Those verbs only appear in S1 free-traversal and the Phase 4 sweep inventory. That means the plan can spend the bulk of remediation budget on collapsed folders and cadence timers while open/run dead controls are “fix-or-document” leftovers. From a capital view, you are funding second-order chrome before the verbs the North Star names first. Add first-class open/run waves (or an explicit inventory row proving they already work end-to-end with transcripts) before funding SC-7/SC-8.

findings.section: Phase 2 stop-time inventory; Phase 4 stop-summary wave
findings.criterion: stop, and restart real Anchor work … without meeting a dead control
findings.message: If stop-time inventory finds nothing meaningful retained, the draft escalates to “checkpoint partial state during runs” — “a larger separately-planned wave” with sizing deferred. Stop-summary then depends on that wave. There is no size cap, no decision deadline, and no honest fallback that still satisfies “stopping leaves a tile summarizing in-flight work” if checkpointing is declined. That is an open-ended option to never finish stop/restart under budget pressure. Pre-write the kill switch: either fund checkpointing inside this effort with a fixed scope, or ship a named thin summary state that does not claim retained work it does not have — and treat full checkpointing as renegotiated out-of-effort, not an infinite dependency.

findings.section: Phase 1 cost_state isolation; rollup spot-check policy; Phase 3 cost_state migration deferred
findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars … unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero
findings.message: Phase 0 pre-decides that wrong rollups may “block,” “ship behind a provisional data label,” or “spin out” — chosen before seeing numbers, but still allowing a ship path that is not full honesty. Separately, if branch isolation rejects the additive column, the plan says cost honesty “cannot be fully met” and may be scoped down rather than met “cosmetically at the render layer.” A bored investor hears two legal paths to partial cost truth while success criteria still promise cost_usd==0 never renders as $0.00 and unmeasured never looks like zero. “Provisional” and “scoped down” are not defined against fabricate-vs-unknown. Lock a single fail-closed rule: no dollar amount renders unless cost_state is measured; subscription/free/unmeasured/failed are labels without fabricated $; provisional is forbidden as a display class unless it is identical to unmeasured/unknown and never a dollar figure.

findings.topic: S1 fail does not reopen build
findings.section: Phase 6 S1; deferred remediation of S1 findings
findings.criterion: Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build
findings.message: S1 is correctly the only gate authorized to declare the North Star met, and status stays “ten criteria met; North Star pending S1.” But S1 findings are explicitly not remediated in this effort — they are routed as follow-on under renegotiation. That means the plan can manufacture a permanent parking state: automated GREEN, S1 failed or never clean, North Star never claimed, and no obligation to burn the remaining capital to close the gap S1 found. A steward proof that cannot force a fix loop is theater with a timestamp. Specify that a failed S1 either (a) reopens named waves inside this effort until S1 passes or John logs a North-Star amendment, or (b) terminal status is “effort failed North Star” — not an indefinite “pending S1” that looks like almost-done.

findings.topic: no ceiling on build-it / aggregate expansion
findings.section: Phase 2 conditional scope-change; three-way reclassification ‘build it’; intro dependency order
findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: Empty rollups flip a surface wave into “aggregate + surface” as a new wave; ABSENT capabilities each get their own wave; stop may spawn checkpointing; coverage may spawn a toolchain wave. None of these expansions has a total-wave ceiling, a cut-line, or a “prefer named unavailable over unbounded build” default for non-core surfaces. Under real budget, expansion waves crowd out Doctor, attach, and cost honesty — the exact surfaces the North Star names. Write a hard expansion budget (max new waves / max reclassified build-its without renegotiation) and a priority order that always funds attach, Doctor, stop/restart, and cost honesty before projects-collapsed, cadence polish, or opportunistic aggregation.

findings.section: Phase 1 shared-artifact ledger; collaborator smoke-check protocol; Phase 4/5 checklist lines
findings.criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
findings.message: Isolation is “named per artifact” and collaborator smoke is “triggered after any wave that modified a shared artifact.” The draft never says what happens if the named collaborator is unavailable, late, or the check is skipped: block the wave, block the release, or note “smoke not run.” A process field with no fail-closed outcome is a checkbox investors ignore and builds skip. Without a mechanical block on shared-artifact writes until smoke returns pass (or John signs a written isolation exception), “nothing ships to v1.1.x” remains an aspiration the EXECUTION-LOG can paper over with an empty field.

findings.section: Phase 5 proxy reconciliation; Phase 2 control-and-surface sweep; intro Phase 4
findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: The draft admits the ten criteria are a proxy and that the North Star is wider, then postpones “narrow the North Star or fund the sweep” until Phase 4 — after all surface waves. That is decision order inverted: you spend the remediation budget on the proxy set, then ask whether the North Star still applies. A bored investor funds one scope, once. Force the narrow-or-fund choice in Phase 0/1 before surface waves are written; otherwise Phase 4 “document with reason” will launder out-of-criteria health/usage/diagnose surfaces as accepted debt while John still hits mislabelled empties S1 is told to treat as findings.

findings.section: Phase 1 transcripts; Phase 0 verification task confirmation; Phase 6 S1
findings.criterion: open, run, stop, restart … Doctor … session attach … S1 … not a silent claim of this build
findings.message: EXISTS verdicts require live transcripts against John’s real v1.2 environment; rollup evidence needs his DB rows; the verification task needs his dated confirmation; S1 is John-only free traversal. The plan has no SLA, no parallel path, and no “blocked on human evidence” clock that forces renegotiation rather than idle swarm spend. If John is the critical path for every honesty claim, the build either fabricates evidence from code-reading (forbidden) or burns calendar with zero surface progress. Name max wait, who can produce transcripts besides John, and what ships as “unknown / not verified” rather than waiting forever for the perfect paste.

findings.section: Phase 2 inventory scope; Phase 4 surface waves; Phase 5 audit
findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: Usage and diagnose get dedicated waves, accessors, taxonomies, and fault sets. “Health” appears in the North Star and the Phase 4/5 sweep language but never receives a first-class inventory column, rollup evidence gate, or surface wave of its own. Health can therefore remain a silent or mislabelled surface until a late audit documents it. Either promote health to the same evidence-and-surface bar as usage/diagnose or strike it from what this effort claims — do not leave it as the unpaid third noun.

findings.topic: dual profile after inventory still John-bound
findings.section: Phase 4 dual-profile verification standard
findings.criterion: without meeting a dead control, a silent zero, a mislabelled empty
findings.message: UI-state fixes must pass on John’s existing profile, not only a clean profile — correct for preference/collapse bugs, but it makes every UI wave depend on access to his real stored state with no fixture that reproduces that profile. Without a captured profile snapshot as a first-class Phase 0 artifact, dual-profile is another serial John dependency that can stall or be quietly skipped. Capture and version the profile fixture when the verification task is named, or the dual-profile gate is not mechanically producible.
